name: Green FRONTIER titles (animal tails)
description: White fuselage; 'FRONTIER' in huge, heavy, slanted green capitals over the forward windows; a thin teal line from an arrow point under the cockpit runs aft below the windows, ending in a short teal bar behind the wing under 'FLYFRONTIER.COM'; each aircraft's fin is a photographic North American animal on a sky-blue background, the sky and clouds running down onto the rear fuselage round the aft door; green engines with a wide teal inlet ring.

logos.description: A photographic North American animal (each aircraft its own: a pronghorn, a warbler, a bear, a fox...) standing or perched on the fin, facing forward, on a sky-blue background with clouds; its name is written under the cockpit.
A small US flag after the registration over the rear windows.

titles.style: Frontier's wordmark: very heavy, slanted, squarish capitals in green (the F's arm cut to a sharp point), across the forward windows from behind the door to the wing.
The web address in small slanted capitals above the teal bar: 'FLY' and '.COM' lighter gray-green, 'FRONTIER' bold green.

notes: Drawn from N638FR (A321neo, June 2025, nearly side-on) and checked on N655FR (Sept 2026). The fin and the sky round the aft door are photographic artwork that differs per aircraft: only its sky background is drawn. The animal's name under the cockpit isn't drawn. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on N638FR (near side-on), cross-checked on N655FR: 'FRONTIER' runs x 0.133 to 0.449, its 'IE' over the second door and the 'R' well past it (it had been drawn ending at that door), cap height from 0.9 m below to 0.7 m above the window line's middle (y -0.11 to 0.48; it had been drawn reaching nearly to the crown); the web address 0.628 to 0.726. Measured on the A321neo, the commonest type in the fleet now; on an A320neo the title ends about over the overwing exits.
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximate standard (a few colors from memory). It followed the 2001 Airbus-era livery (Wikipedia); the animal tails were kept. Year of introduction not confirmed from a dated source, so 'from' is left empty.
